subsystems.name: Preform and feed system
subsystems.role: supplies ultra-pure fluoride glass to the melt without introducing crystals or bubbles.

subsystems.name: Melting and drawing furnace
subsystems.role: melts the preform and pulls a continuous filament.

subsystems.name: Cooling and coating
subsystems.role: solidifies the fibre without crystallisation and protects it from handling damage.

subsystems.name: Spooling and tension control
subsystems.role: winds the fibre onto a spool at a steady tension so it does not break or deform.

subsystems.name: Environmental control and vibration isolation
subsystems.role: maintains a clean, low-vibration vacuum or inert atmosphere around the draw.

subsystems.name: Return and packaging
subsystems.role: prepares the spool for re-entry and recovery as high-value downmass.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise ultra-pure ZBLAN glass
buildSteps.detail: Mix high-purity fluoride powders (zirconium, barium, lanthanum, aluminium and sodium fluorides) in a dry, oxygen-free atmosphere to avoid water and oxide contamination. Melt and quench the mixture into a glass preform.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the preform
buildSteps.detail: Cast or extrude the glass into a rod or crucible shape, then polish and clean it so no surface crystals seed during drawing.

buildSteps.title: Launch and load
buildSteps.detail: Transport the preform to the microgravity platform and load it into the draw tower inside a sealed, clean enclosure.

buildSteps.title: Melt the preform
buildSteps.detail: Heat the preform in the furnace until it softens. In free fall there are no buoyancy-driven convection currents to stir the melt, so the glass stays homogeneous and crystal-free.

buildSteps.title: Draw the fibre
buildSteps.detail: Pull a thin filament from the molten zone at a controlled rate. Surface tension and viscosity set the diameter, which is monitored continuously.

buildSteps.title: Cool and coat
buildSteps.detail: Pass the fibre through a controlled cooling zone to solidify it without crystallisation, then apply a protective polymer coating and cure it.

buildSteps.title: Spool and inspect
buildSteps.detail: Wind the fibre onto a spool under steady tension, checking diameter and tension to catch defects early.

buildSteps.title: Return to Earth
buildSteps.detail: Package the spool in a return capsule, re-enter, and recover it. The short fibre length is the high-value downmass.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Measure optical loss, strength and uniformity, then splice or connectorise the fibre for telecom or sensing use.

prerequisites.why: the International Space Station provides long-duration free fall today, and commercial stations are being developed.
terrestrial ZBLAN fibre exists, but preforms pure enough for theoretical low loss are not routinely produced.
draw towers have been demonstrated on the ISS, but only for short lengths and limited runs.
cargo capsules regularly return from the ISS, so spools of fibre can come back to Earth.
test equipment and fusion splicers for fluoride fibre are available, though handling remains delicate.

pathway.milestone: ISS experiments drawing short lengths of ZBLAN fibre and measuring losses well below conventional silica fibre
pathway.unlocks: proof that microgravity suppresses the crystallisation that limits terrestrial ZBLAN.

pathway.milestone: commercial production on the ISS or early commercial LEO stations, selling fibre to specialty telecom and sensing customers
pathway.unlocks: first revenue and real operating experience.

pathway.milestone: scaling to longer fibre lengths and higher volume with automated draw and spooling
pathway.unlocks: lower cost per metre and wider adoption in long-haul links and sensors.

pathway.milestone: dedicated in-space fibre factories with continuous production and regular return flights
pathway.unlocks: ultra-low-loss fibre as a routine product, competing with silica in niche high-value applications.
